result.topic_en: A remark that mathematicians should simplify rather than generalize, followed by a proof that an invariant's multiplier is a power of the substitution determinant, a statement on divisors of modules under perturbation, and a statement with proof sketch on the finiteness of invariants of a single linear transformation.

items.english: If the module (F_1 + εG_1, F_2 + εG_2, ..., F_m + εG_m) has a divisor of order N for arbitrarily small ε, then for ε = 0 it certainly has a divisor whose order is not less than N.

items.english: If a single linear transformation x_i' = α_i1 x_1 + ... + α_in x_n is given (i = 1, 2 ... n), then there is a finite number of invariants (J(x_1...x_n) = J(x_1'...x_n')) in terms of which all others can be expressed integrally and rationally.
